T1.implementation_approach: Use a component-based design approach with a focus on user experience. Create wireframes and prototypes using design tools, then implement using a frontend framework.
T1.notes: Ensure the UI is intuitive and supports search, filter, and sort functionalities.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs to handle problem creation, retrieval, updating, and deletion. Use MVC architecture for backend development.
T2.notes: Ensure proper validation and error handling for API endpoints.

T3.implementation_approach: Design a relational or NoSQL database schema to store problem details, tags, difficulty levels, and metadata.
T3.notes: Optimize schema for search and filtering operations.

T4.implementation_approach: Design a form-based interface for users to submit code. Include features like code editor, language selection, and submission button.
T4.notes: Ensure the editor supports syntax highlighting and error detection.

T5.implementation_approach: Implement a sandboxed environment to execute user-submitted code securely. Compare outputs with expected results.
T5.notes: Focus on security and scalability of the evaluation system.

T6.implementation_approach: Design a profile page to display user details, achievements, and activity history. Use responsive design principles.
T6.notes: Include options for users to edit their profile information.

T7.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to handle user profile creation, retrieval, updating, and deletion. Use authentication and authorization mechanisms.
T7.notes: Ensure secure handling of sensitive user data.

T8.implementation_approach: Design a leaderboard interface to display top users based on scores or activity. Include sorting and filtering options.
T8.notes: Ensure real-time updates for leaderboard rankings.

T9.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to fetch and update leaderboard data. Use caching for performance optimization.

T10.implementation_approach: Design an interface to display hints and tutorials for problems. Include a collapsible or modal-based design.
T10.notes: Ensure hints are displayed contextually and do not reveal full solutions.

T11.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage hints and tutorials. Include endpoints for creation, retrieval, updating, and deletion.
T11.notes: Ensure hints and tutorials are linked to specific problems.

T12.implementation_approach: Write unit and integration tests for the problem library functionality. Use mock data for testing.
T12.notes: Focus on edge cases and API response validation.

T13.implementation_approach: Test the code submission and evaluation system using various test cases, including edge cases and invalid inputs.
T13.notes: Ensure the system handles malicious code securely.

T14.implementation_approach: Test user profile functionalities, including creation, updates, and data retrieval. Validate authentication and authorization.
T14.notes: Ensure secure handling of user data during testing.

T15.implementation_approach: Test leaderboard functionalities, including data retrieval, sorting, and filtering. Use performance testing for large datasets.
T15.notes: Focus on real-time updates and caching mechanisms.

T16.implementation_approach: Test hints and tutorials functionalities, including creation, retrieval, and linking to problems.
T16.notes: Ensure hints are displayed correctly and do not reveal full solutions.

T17.implementation_approach: Deploy the platform using a cloud service provider. Set up CI/CD pipelines for automated deployment.
T17.notes: Ensure scalability, security, and monitoring of the deployed platform.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

# Initialize the SQLAlchemy instance
db = SQLAlchemy()

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, server_default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, server_default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    def __init__(self, title, description, difficulty):
        self.title = title
        self.description = description
        self.difficulty = difficulty

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<Problem {self.id} - {self.title}>'

from app.database import db

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), unique=True, nullable=False)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<User {self.username}>'

from app.database import db

class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    language = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    result = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=True)
    submitted_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now())

    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=False)
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('problems.id'), nullable=False)

    user = db.relationship('User', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))
    problem = db.relationship('Problem', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))

    def __init__(self, code, language, user_id, problem_id, result=None):
        self.code = code
        self.language = language
        self.user_id = user_id
        self.problem_id = problem_id
        self.result = result

    def save(self):
        db.session.add(self)
        db.session.commit()

    def delete(self):
        db.session.delete(self)
        db.session.commit()

from flask import Blueprint
from app.models.problem import Problem

def problem_blueprint():
    blueprint = Blueprint('problem', __name__)

    @blueprint.route('/problems', methods=['GET'])
    def get_all_problems():
        """
        Route to retrieve all problems.
        """
        # Simulating problem retrieval, assuming Problem.query.all() fetches all problems
        problems = Problem.query.all()
        problems_data = [{"id": problem.id, "title": problem.title, "description": problem.description} for problem in problems]
        return {"problems": problems_data}, 200

    @blueprint.route('/problem/<int:problem_id>', methods=['GET'])
    def get_problem_by_id(problem_id):
        """
        Route to retrieve a problem by its ID.
        """
        # Simulating problem retrieval, assuming Problem.query.get() fetches by ID
        problem = Problem.query.get(problem_id)
        if problem:
            return {"id": problem.id, "title": problem.title, "description": problem.description}, 200
        return {"error": "Problem not found"}, 404

    return blueprint

__all__ = ['blueprints']

from flask import Flask
from app.routes import *
from app.database import db
from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_blueprint
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_blueprint
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_blueprint

def create_app():
    # Initialize the Flask app
    app = Flask(__name__)

    # Configure app settings if needed
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///app.db'  # Example configuration
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False

    # Initialize the database
    db.init_app(app)

    # Register blueprints
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint, url_prefix='/problems')
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint, url_prefix='/users')
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint, url_prefix='/solutions')

    return app

from app import create_app

# Entry point for the ACM Problem-Solving Platform
app = create_app()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run()

# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A website designed to help users solve ACM-style competitive programming problems.

## Features

- Problem Library: A comprehensive library of ACM-style problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Submission and Evaluation: Allows users to submit code solutions and receive instant feedback on correctness and performance.
- User Profiles: Enables users to create profiles to track their progress, solved problems, and rankings.
- Leaderboard: Displays rankings of users based on their problem-solving performance.
- Hints and Tutorials: Provides hints and tutorials for selected problems to help users improve their skills.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
